privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This Privacy Policy explains what happens to the data of people using verminew.github.io and its order form.
privacy.puodoNote: You may also lodge a complaint with the President of the Polish Personal Data Protection Office:

sections.title: Data controller
paragraphs: The controller of your personal data is Michał Oślizło.
For privacy or personal-data matters, email: {{adminEmail}}.

sections.title: How the order form works
paragraphs: The form runs locally in your browser. The data you enter is not automatically sent to a server or to me.
When you download the ZIP package, it is created on your device. Sending it by email is your separate and voluntary decision.
list: Site preferences such as theme, language and animation settings may be saved in localStorage.
A form draft may be saved in sessionStorage only for the current browser session.
You can remove this data at any time by clearing the website data in your browser settings.

sections.title: When you contact me
paragraphs: If you voluntarily send an email, I receive only the data and attachments that you choose to include.
I use this data to reply, continue correspondence and, if you ask, discuss potential collaboration.
list: The legal basis is art. 6(1)(b) GDPR when your message concerns steps before a possible contract at your request.
Otherwise, the legal basis is art. 6(1)(f) GDPR: my legitimate interest in replying and handling correspondence.
Providing data is voluntary, but I cannot reply without contact details.

sections.title: Hosting and external services
paragraphs: The site is hosted on GitHub Pages and loads fonts from Google Fonts. Your browser connects to these services when you open the site.
External services process data under their own privacy policies. I do not use them for advertising or my own analytics.
list: GitHub Pages — website hosting; GitHub may process technical connection data, including IP address, for service security.
Google Fonts — font provider; a font request may include IP address and technical browser data.
Proton Mail — email provider; it processes message content only after an email is sent to {{adminEmail}}.

sections.title: Retention
paragraphs: The website does not store form data on a server.
I keep emails only for as long as needed to reply and finish contact, normally no longer than 12 months from the last message, unless further retention is necessary to defend against claims.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: Depending on the legal basis, you may have the following rights:
list: Right to object to processing based on legitimate interests (art. 21 GDPR)
Right to data portability where the conditions of art. 20 GDPR are met

sections.title: Cookies and browser storage
paragraphs: The site does not use its own advertising or analytics cookies.
GitHub Pages and Google Fonts may use their own technical mechanisms under their privacy policies.

sections.title: No profiling
paragraphs: Your data is not used for profiling or automated decision-making (art. 22 GDPR).

questions.question: How much does a website cost?
questions.answer: It depends on scope. A simple landing page is around €120–350, a standard site €120–350, a web app with a dashboard or store €350–1 000, larger projects are quoted individually. The order form is the fastest way to get a concrete quote.

questions.question: How does working together actually go?
questions.answer: 1. You send the order form. 2. I come back with questions or a quote. 3. We agree on scope, timeline and terms. 4. You pay 50% upfront. 5. I build it with regular updates. 6. You accept, pay the remaining 50%, I hand over the code.

questions.question: How long does it take?
questions.answer: A simple site — 1–3 weeks. A web app — 1–3 months. Depends on scope, availability of materials and the current queue. We agree on a timeline before we start and I stick to it.

questions.question: Do you work alone?
questions.answer: Yes, with AI as a tool. For most projects in my range that's enough. If a project needs something I genuinely can't deliver, I'll say so upfront instead of overpromising.

questions.question: Do you take commercial projects?
questions.answer: Yes. I'm a student so my availability is limited, but I take commercial work seriously. I evaluate each project individually based on whether I can realistically deliver it.

questions.question: What if I need changes after delivery?
questions.answer: Revisions within the agreed scope are free. Changes beyond the original scope or new requirements are quoted separately. We define the scope before we start — that protects both of us.

questions.question: Can you help with hosting and domain?
questions.answer: Yes. I don't sell domains or hosting, but I can help you pick and set them up. For static sites you often don't need paid hosting at all (GitHub Pages, Vercel).

questions.question: What technologies do you use?
questions.answer: Mainly React + TypeScript for frontend, Python or PHP for backend. I try to match the tech to the project, not the other way around. If you have stack requirements, mention them and I'll check if I can deliver.

questions.question: Will I get the source code?
questions.answer: Yes — full code and copyright transfer on final payment. Do whatever you want with it.

questions.question: How do I reach you?
questions.answer: Email (werminew@protonmail.com) or Discord. I usually reply within 24–48 hours, on workdays between 4 PM and 8 PM CET.
